rows.verified: Landlords are responsible for the safety of tenants in relation to gas appliances, fittings and flues they provide.
The legal duty covers provided appliances, associated fittings, flues and pipework.
Communal gas appliances, flues and pipework used by tenants are included in safety arrangements.
Maintenance and repair of landlord-provided gas equipment must be arranged through a Gas Safe registered engineer.
Landlords must arrange a gas safety check every twelve months.
The gas safety check record must be retained for two years.
Existing tenants must receive a copy within 28 days after the check is completed.
New tenants must receive the gas safety record before moving in.

rows.source: HSE gas safety check qualification guidance
rows.verified: A registered engineer cannot legitimately sign off gas work performed by an unregistered installer.

rows.source: HSE gas safety check qualification guidance
rows.verified: Consumers should verify both Gas Safe registration and qualification for the specific work shown on the engineer's card.
A record must identify the description and location of each appliance or flue checked.
A record must include the engineer's name, registration number, signature and check date.
The record must state safety defects identified and remedial action taken.
Electronic records are allowed if reproducible, protected from loss or interference and able to identify the engineer.
For a suspected leak, HSE directs people to call the gas emergency service, open doors and windows and shut off supply when safe and known.
HSE states that around seven people die each year from gas-related carbon-monoxide poisoning; the value is approximate national context.
Carbon monoxide cannot be seen, tasted or smelled and can kill quickly without warning.
Poor installation or maintenance can create fire, explosion, gas-leak and carbon-monoxide risks; workplaces must use appropriately registered or competent people.
